scenario: A real estate analytics firm tracks only properties sold above $200,000 â€” sales below that threshold are excluded as 'distressed' and handled by a separate team. An economist uses the firm's average to report on housing market health.

data.description: Database includes only property sales > $200k. Sale prices assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = $150k.

question: Tracked sales average $380k. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean property sale price Î¼ across all sales (including distressed), and (b) the fraction of all sales that appear in the database.
naive_answer: The average property sells for approximately $380k since that is the database figure.

python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(200-mu)/150; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+150*norm.pdf(a)/sf-380 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,100,379)
assert abs(mu-328)<5
assert abs(norm.sf((200-mu)/150)-0.8040)<0.01
